paragraphs.text: Ruicaokui (瑞草魁) is a [green tea](green:definition) from [Anhui](anhui:where-it-is), the province in eastern China where tea grows only in the hills of the south and west, in a few separate pockets, while the flat north grows none. Anhui is [known above all for its green teas](anhui:known-for). Its tea hills lie under [mist and cloud](anhui:land-and-climate) for much of the year, and the cold winters let the bushes rest, so the leaf comes on strong in spring.

Like every tea of its kind, this leaf was never allowed to oxidise. Soon after picking it was [fixed](green:making), heated fast to stop the leaf's own enzymes before they could turn it brown. It was then rolled to take its shape and dried until only a little water remained, so that it keeps.

brewing.text: Green tea takes water well below the boil, about 80°C, a little cooler for the youngest leaf and a little warmer for older, larger leaf. Boiling water draws out bitterness and dries the cup. A common start is about 2 grams of leaf to 100 ml, in a glass or a small gaiwan, with short steeps of half a minute to two minutes, and the same leaf can be brewed a few times.

notice.text: A fresh, clean cup that many call crisp, with a sweet, soft finish, and a pale green to yellow-green liquor. The smell runs from fresh leaf to flowers, and steamed teas lean grassy or seaweed-like. Too much heat or too long a steep turns the cup bitter and drying.
